reviewer: provider_contract (independent of roadmap and Gate A implementation)
scope: Behavioral regression tests using Node VM DOM stubs and isolated temporary repository copies. No real browser rendering or native UI execution is claimed by this review.
html_hash_rule: Read design/projectos-live-mvp-roadmap.html as UTF-8, replace the entire STATUS_SNAPSHOT_START through STATUS_SNAPSHOT_END comment block with <!-- STATUS_SNAPSHOT_EXCLUDED -->, then SHA-256. This excludes regenerated status data while binding reviewed code and layout.
verified: Inline JavaScript compiles; literal getElementById references exist and HTML IDs are unique.
Imported malicious note/evidence markup is escaped before render interpolation.
Agent manifests cannot set human-only tasks accepted or verified; locked checkbox events cannot accept them.
Manual acceptance restores only for the same fully verified candidate revision.
A different source revision clears manual acceptance and previous nonbaseline QA verification.
Mismatched served source snapshot does not apply an unbound status manifest.
Fresh failing Gate A, D and E reports block promotion.
Missing source hashes prevent an implemented evidence claim.
Changing source changes source revision and blocks stale source-hashed reports.
Server refresh regenerates on code changes and skips unchanged fingerprints, tested without opening a socket.

gate_a_review.duplicate_cancel_registration: Atomic mutex registration rejects duplicate active ID without replacing original Arc; regression test verifies retained handle identity.
gate_a_review.job_bound: Atomic registration enforces at most 16 active jobs.
gate_a_review.native_build_evidence: Recorded cargo regression tests and debug bundle build succeeded; independently checked report source hashes and built binary SHA-256. Did not rerun the native build or UI in this review.

limitations: VM DOM stubs do not execute HTML event attributes or prove browser CSP, accessibility, appearance or real user interactions.
Server refresh logic is executed in a VM against temporary filesystem fixtures, not an actual HTTP socket.
These checks protect imported data and revision semantics; they are not an authentication boundary against arbitrary code running in the same local browser origin.
Final manual user acceptance, clean-machine installation and full platform matrix remain outstanding.
